topic: SDK Landlock TSYNC consumers and per-thread isolation assumptions
status: final conservative API-retention decision; runtime necessity and behavior unconfirmed
evidence: SDK runtime use of TSYNC is unconfirmed. Searches of pinned system, bionic, frameworks, packages and device trees located generic syscall exposure and generated/prebuilt names, but no definite TSYNC caller. This does not prove it is unnecessary: retain this configured generic userspace security interface conservatively, without adding a future platform. Broader per-application assumptions about thread isolation and runtime scheduling behavior remain unverified. TSYNC intentionally replaces sibling Landlock domains and logging state irrespective of existing restrictions. A less restricted sibling can therefore relax another sibling Landlock configuration. Preserve this explicit opt-in ACK API for compatibility, with sibling threads sharing policy authority; do not describe it as monotonic per-thread confinement. The caller still must satisfy native no_new_privs or CAP_SYS_ADMIN checks, ruleset validation/merging and maximum layer rules. No-new-privs is propagated when set and never cleared. Different credentials are prepared from each sibling and only the Landlock blob is replaced; identical credentials may share the new credential reference. Native other-LSM checks and filesystem/network access checks remain. Allocation failure, signal cancellation and serialized retry were source-reviewed, not concurrency-tested.

Complete revert and original fix reviewed; current loop.c is whole LTS apart from the separately reviewed namespace import. STATX_DIOALIGN prevents enabling an I/O geometry smaller than filesystem requirements, including out-of-place and multi-device cases; backing-device sectors alone cannot guarantee this. The actual local LTP test assumes BLKSSZGET suffices and can fail with EINVAL under this deliberate native policy. Android libdm requests 4096 blocks before enabling DIO; fs_mgr zram and image-manager users propagate failures, so compatibility for files with larger/no DIO alignment is not asserted. apexd requests 4096 blocks and current source copies li before adding its DIRECT_IO flag; do not misrepresent that flag as passed by this branch. Native configure can clear incompatible DIO while explicit SET_DIRECT_IO rejects it. Preserve upstream correctness rather than report success for unsupported direct I/O. Exact runtime necessity of ACK test behavior remains unconfirmed; no LTP/loop runtime performed.
